# Published hard-to-round inputs for log10, one double per line as its raw bits in hex
# (Double.doubleToRawLongBits), read by Inputs.hardCases("log10"). Lines starting with # are
# comments. Only the input values are taken from the sources below; they are numeric facts.
#
# At such an input the exact log10(x) lies unusually close to a rounding boundary of binary64
# (a midpoint between two doubles for round-to-nearest, a double itself for the directed
# modes), so an implementation's last few rounding errors decide which double it returns. For a
# port that follows fdlibm's operations exactly they are no harder than any other input; their
# use here is that a dropped correction term or a reassociated sum, a change far below one ulp,
# is most likely to flip the result exactly at these points.
#
# Section 1: V. Lefevre, hard-to-round cases in round-to-nearest, file testlibm-data (updated
# 2020-11-27), https://www.vinc17.net/research/testlibm/testlibm-data.xz, from the page
# https://www.vinc17.net/research/testlibm/, which states no licence or reuse terms. Every
# line for "l10" in mode N, in the file's order. Each line was rechecked with
# 400-digit decimal arithmetic: the file's result is log10(x) rounded to nearest, and the
# file's direction bit agrees. Measured at the same time: of these 1883 inputs, 1307 have
# at least 40 bits after the round bit pointing at the midpoint (the exact result within 2^-41
# ulp of it), 329 have 20 to 39 and 247 fewer than 20.
